results.title: SWE-Trail: History-Guided Trajectory Collection for Coding Agent Training
results.snippet: Coding agents solve repository issues through long sequences of exploration, editing, and validation. These trajectories are increasingly used as post-training data, so how they are collected shapes what the trained model learns. A common approach is to sample multiple trajectories independently for each issue and then select or curate them. However, as more trajectories are sampled independently, later trajectories become increasingly redundant, even though earlier trajectories could guide where subsequent collection effort should be spent. A natural way to use this history is to expose it t…

results.title: SWE-ABS: Adversarial Benchmark Strengthening Exposes Inflated Success Rates on Test-based Benchmark
results.snippet: The SWE-Bench Verified leaderboard is approaching saturation, with the top system achieving 78.80%. However, we show that this performance is inflated. Our re-evaluation reveals that one in five "solved" patches from the top-30 agents are semantically incorrect, passing only because weak test suites fail to expose their errors. We present SWE-ABS, an adversarial framework that strengthens test suites through a two-stage pipeline: (1) coverage-driven augmentation using program slicing to target untested code regions, and (2) mutation-driven adversarial testing that synthesizes plausible but in…

results.title: SWE-Bench Pro V2: A Cleaner, Harder-to-Game Coding Benchmark
results.snippet: SWE-Bench Pro is a widely used benchmark of long-horizon software engineering tasks for coding agents. As agents improve, they reach task issues earlier agents never touched and interact with the evaluation environment in ways the original harness did not anticipate. We present SWE-Bench Pro V2, a revised public split built to keep the benchmark accurate as capabilities advance. results.snippet: This paper presents the overview of the AuTexTification shared task as part of the IberLEF 2023 Workshop in Iberian Languages Evaluation Forum, within the framework of the SEPLN 2023 conference. AuTexTification consists of two subtasks: for Subtask 1, participants had to determine whether a text is human-authored or has been generated by a large language model. For Subtask 2, participants had to attribute a machine-generated text to one of six different text generation models. report_md:
# Agent 评测与欺骗（能力基准、欺骗、可纠正性）深度调研报告

**日期**：2026-11-22（UTC）  
**领域**：Agent Evaluation & Deception / Corrigibility（具身智能·大模型评测·对齐安全）  
**检索源数量**：34 条可引用证据（[1]–[2]）

---

## 1. 进展与热点

### 1.1 编码 Agent 基准的“去饱和化”竞赛（2025–2026）
- **SWE-Bench Verified 接近饱和**（Top-1 78.80%），但 **SWE-ABS** 通过对抗性加强测试集揭示：Top-30 系统中 **1/5 “解决”补丁在语义上不正确**，仅因弱测试套件通过 [3]。  
- **SWE-Bench Pro V2** 重构评测 harness，修复环境交互漏洞，提供“更难作弊”的长程软工任务 [4]。  
- **Saving SWE-Bench** 提出基准变异方法，将 GitHub Issue 转为 IDE 交互式对话场景，缩小“离线评测 vs 真实开发流”的分布偏移 [5]。  
- **SWE-Trail** 引入历史轨迹引导的轨迹采集，用于 Coding Agent 后训练数据构建，强调轨迹质量对策略学习的决定性影响 [6]。  
- **SWE-MERA** 推出动态评测框架，支持 Agentic 评测而非静态打分 [7]。

> **增量判断**：2025–2026 年编码 Agent 评测从“静态通过率竞赛”转向“对抗鲁棒性、环境真实性、轨迹质量、动态评测”四大维度的系统性升级。

| 关键进展 | 年份 | 机构/来源 | 热度证据 | 权威证据 | 关注度 | 推荐度 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## 2. 工业界与产品

### 2.1 主流编码 Agent 产品与基准绑定现状
- **SWE-Bench 系列** 已成为 GitHub Copilot、Cursor、Devin、Factory 等编码 Agent 产品的**事实标准榜单** [14][3][4]。  
- **SWE-Bench Goes Live!** 推动榜单常态化运营，支持实时提交与复现 [14]。  
- 产业界普遍面临“榜单高分 ≠ 真实 IDE 解决力”的**部署落差**，催生 Saving SWE-Bench 等变异评测 [5]。

### 2.2 通用 Agent 框架的评测模块化进展
- **LangChain/LangGraph**、**AutoGPT**、**OpenAI Evals** 等框架均内置评测接口，但缺乏**统一的欺骗/可纠正性评测插件** [11][8]。  
- **AgentBench** 曾尝试统一多环境评测，但近两年维护频度下降，社区呼吁“评测即服务”标准化 [11]。

> **不确定**：目前无公开证据显示头部厂商（OpenAI、Anthropic、Google DeepMind）已将欺骗检测、可关闭性测试纳入常规发布门控流程。> 待核实
